content:
maria_support: Hey team — AcmeHealth just escalated. They reported 3x latency to our API this morning and intermittent 503s. They say traffic was supposed to hit their EU dedicated pool but traces show calls going to hosted-us. Billing also shows spike on hosted. Can someone triage?

sam_infra: Thanks Maria. Do we have the customer's region pin metadata and a sample request ID?

maria_support: Customer id = acct-4589, example request id = req_20260317_8f3a. They say this started at ~08:12 UTC.

nisha_eng: Pulling routing logs now. Quick note: we rolled a small routing change around 07:50 UTC yesterday (rate-limit backfill heuristics). Could be related.

zoe_sre: I've got the proxy traces for req_20260317_8f3a — upstream selection shows fallback to hosted-us after pin lookup returned empty for tenant region. Stack: edge -> router -> hosted-us pool.

sam_infra: Can you paste the router debug span here?

zoe_sre: Sure — snippet from router logs (sanitized):

```
[2026-03-17T08:12:05Z] tenant=acct-4589 pin_lookup=MISS ttl=expired?=true backend_choice=hosted-us reason=pin-miss-fallback
[2026-03-17T08:12:05Z] fallback_policy=allow_hosted capacity_check=passed
[2026-03-17T08:12:05Z] auth_token=jwtxxx... exp=2026-03-17T08:11:30Z auth_status=EXPIRED -> refresh_attempt=skipped
[2026-03-17T08:12:05Z] route_complete target=hosted-us latency_ms=720 status=503
```

nisha_eng: Interesting — token expiration logged before the request. If auth refresh is skipped, router may treat tenant as unauthenticated for dedicated routing and allow fallback. We recently tightened auth checks in the pin resolver.

jordan_prod: AcmeHealth claims they rotated their KMS keys last week. Could token lifetimes differ if they rotated keys? billing_bot: FYI — hosted billing shows a burst of 14k tokens for acct-4589 at 08:12-08:18 UTC.

sam_infra: Two hypotheses: 1) Pin TTL expired and pin resolver rejected on auth token expiry leading to fallback; 2) Pin resolver had a transient store miss (etcd) and fallback took effect. We need repro steps.

maria_support: Customer is willing to run a trace if we provide steps. They said they saw 503s and higher p99 latency ~1s -> 700ms to hosted-us which is bad for EU customers.

nisha_eng: Repro plan: ask Acme to run a single request with header `X-Debug-Req: true` and include request id. We can instrument the pin resolver to log full decision path. Also ask them to send the auth token header used.

zoe_sre: I'll enable verbose pin resolver logs for tenant acct-4589 for 30 minutes. Command: `kubectl logs -l app=pin-resolver -c resolver --since=1h | grep acct-4589` and I'll attach trace id mapping.

sam_infra: Also check router config for fallback_policy for that tenant: `GET /admin/tenants/acct-4589/policy` should show pinned_region and fallback flag. If pinned_region present but fallback=allow_hosted that's wrong — should be `deny_hosted` for Dedicated customers.

jordan_prod: We had a recent migration that defaulted missing policy entries to allow_hosted for 24h to avoid hard errors for new tenants. That could be why. Who owns the migration?

nisha_eng: That migration is mine — it updated default fallback to allow_hosted if policy absent. But we added an exception for tenants flagged as "dedicated". Maybe flagging didn't stick during the DB migration for some older dedicated customers.

maria_support: AcmeHealth is definitely on dedicated (contract shows Dedicated-EU).

zoe_sre: Patch quick check: If auth token expiry triggers pin lookup to short-circuit and the tenant record is missing dedicated flag, we'll fall back. So we have a two-factor failure: token expired + migration misflag.

sam_infra: Immediate mitigation: temporarily flip their tenant fallback to deny_hosted. I can run: `PATCH /admin/tenants/acct-4589` payload `{ "fallback_policy":"deny_hosted", "pinned_region":"eu-west-1" }`. Anyone object?

jordan_prod: Go ahead. Also confirm we will invalidate any hosted sessions billing-wise.

billing_bot: Note: switching fallback won't retroactively move charges. We'll need to credit the hosted billing spike if we confirm routing fault. Create billing ticket referencing hosted surge.

maria_support: I'll notify Acme and ask for a test after you flip.

sam_infra: Done — policy updated at 08:45 UTC. Please run a verification trace.

maria_support: Acme ran a test at 08:47 with req_id=req_20260317_08_47_test. They report latency back to normal (~55ms) and no 503.

zoe_sre: Router logs for the test show pin_lookup=HIT and route=dedicated-eu target=eu-dedicated-pool latency_ms=48 status=200.

nisha_eng: Root cause summary in-thread: 1) Migration reset the dedicated flag for acct-4589 -> default fallback=allow_hosted. 2) An expired auth token during requests caused the pin resolver to early-decline dedicated routing, triggering fallback. Combined, requests routed to hosted-us.

jordan_prod: Action items: nisha to roll migration fix to backfill dedicated flags for affected customers (run backfill job), sam to add an instrumented alert when fallback-hosted for dedicated tenants exceeds threshold, billing to create credit for Acme, maria to send postmortem + customer update.

nisha_eng: I'll queue a backfill job and target 1h run window. Also adding a safety: if tenant contract indicates dedicated, ignore token expiry in pin decision for up to 10s while triggering an async auth refresh so we don't route incorrectly.

sam_infra: I'll open a quick PR to change default fallback from allow_hosted to deny_hosted for any tenant with a dedicated contract when policy missing. Also add a metric `dedicated_fallback_count` and threshold alert.

maria_support: Thanks team. I'll draft the customer message: apology, explanation, mitigation steps, and offer a credit.

billing_bot: Billing ticket created #BILL-1129 for hosted spike credit review.

opsbot: Incident note: created incident INC-20260317-02, severity=high, owner=nisha_eng, mitigated_by=policy_patch, status=monitoring.

maria_support: I'll follow up with Acme once billing confirms. Closing thread after postmortem doc is posted. :white_check_mark:
